title: Mexican band at the 1885 Cotton Exposition and the Garde Republicaine
summary: The huge Mexican symphonic band in New Orleans, and the French Garde Republicaine heard in World War I at the pier.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: I noticed you say Lorenzo T.O. came with the band Roma.
There was one big band that came up, the Mexican band for the Cotton Exposition in 1885. You don't happen to be... I know you were young.
No, no. I remember that. Yes, I remember that very well. But I don't think, at that time, either one of those T.O.'s were with the outfit. No.
They were already in New Orleans. Oh, there.
Oh, sure. They were already stationed in New Orleans. Before 1885.
Because there was a famous national Mexican band. I have some of the sheet music with a picture of it.
I think Over the Waves was their theme song. They introduced that to New Orleans. They have the picture on the sheet music. It's quite a big band. Oh, yes.

It was a huge thing. It was really a symphonic band. Yes. Because they had cello, bass violins, and all that sort of stuff. Oh, as soon as you see everything in them. Uh-huh. All the things that you find in a regular band, plus the strings. Yes. And the only band that I have heard that compared with that outfit was the God Republic from France.

When they came here during World War I. We were then playing at the pier. And we didn't play the Sunday afternoon that they were to give the concert, because they used the same stage and auditorium where we were. But having been employed there, we were permitted to stay and listen to the concert. One of the most wonderful experiences I've ever had and shall never forget.
